triggerReason: An eligible causal diagnosis still could not be converted into a safe choice among no action and multiple bounded interventions with comparable evidence, resource constraints, stopping rules, and human authorization.
action: Added a strict versioned Intervention DSL, provenance-preserving candidate portfolios, Pareto comparison, paired multi-seed experiment designs, first-sample guardrail stops, deterministic replay, resource-aware isolated scheduling, durable planning decisions, authenticated APIs, and an accessible Planning Workbench.
outcome: NEXUS-7 can now compare no action with at least two distinct synthetic interventions, explain their trade-offs and rejection reasons, stop unsafe experiments immediately, and prevent staging when diagnosis trust, capability, budget, schedule, experiment evidence, or human approvals are missing.
evidence: Every incident plan contains no action and two valid declarative candidates
The strict DSL rejects arbitrary fields, action kinds, capability mismatches, unbounded values, invalid resource claims, and broken inverses
Rule, validated-model, human, and no-action provenance is preserved while equivalent action sets are deduplicated
Every candidate records benefit, cost, risk, synthetic group impacts, Pareto position, dominators, and rejection reasons
Five paired seeds freeze objectives, guardrails, sample windows, stopping rules, Holm-Bonferroni correction, regression-to-mean control, and cycle control
All 225 experiment runs replay deterministically and injected guardrail failures stop at the first sample
Isolated scheduling records budget and resource conflicts instead of contaminating a shared world
High-risk or irreversible candidates declare two distinct human-admin approvals; service accounts cannot approve
Memory and PostgreSQL persist plans, decisions, and append-only causal events through the shared lifecycle contract
Planning Workbench exposes no-action, alternatives, evidence controls, queue reasons, approvals, and the synthetic staging boundary
Planning acceptance, focused unit tests, PostgreSQL round trip, TypeScript, lint, production build, and browser/axe gates pass
